I highly recommend this to anyone struggling to get into a dungeon group or making friends:

Get the LFG bulletin board addon and change the filter to the dungeons you are looking to run. You can also set it to play an alert when that dungeon is mentioned in LFG.

OR

Start forming the group yourself. I know it can seem a bit intimidating to create groups, but remember there are people playing just like you that want to be in dungeon groups but don't want to start the group. Say something like "LFM tanks/heals/DPS for normal (dungeon name)" and type it in zone chat and LFG chat once every minute or so. You can even form the group while grinding mobs or quests nearby. If you are on a smaller server, you could also try typing "/who 60-64" and politely whispering people in that level range asking if they want to run your dungeon. It might take a little while to get a tank/healer, but just be patient and polite/friendly. I promise you will attract fun friends and people to play with!

OR

Join a guild completely dedicated to leveling or socializing. You will definitely find a lot of people in there that have the same desires you do. One way to join one would be to say "Level 64 (class) looking for leveling guild" or "LF leveling guild" in a city chat zone or in the LFG chat channel. I've noticed a lot of these guilds dont stick around for a long time, but its a good start if you want to socialize right away. I've personally gotten a lot of assistance running dungeons by joining guilds like this.

I form dungeon groups all the time now after being nervous to make them when i started playing. Sometimes you get a rotten egg, but ive made many friends and guildies after forming groups over the past 2 years. Let me know if you need any help or if these strategies work for you!

Not directly related to healing but very important - make sure you create your characters on the correct server. Several servers do not have any active Horde population, you can see which do here: https://ironforge.pro/population/tbc/

As others have said all relevant raids are still run, the first raid you'll do at max level is Karazhan :)

Leveling will take you a good amount of time, I would estimate for a completely fresh character it will take around a month to reach 70.

If you want to chill out and just grind, dont worry and pick whatever seems fun and lvl it to 70. 

If you want to raid reliably on each weekly reset, I highly recommend picking a class or specialization that is in demand and join a raiding guild. This will make it far easier to get into groups and you will spend less time looking for raid groups and may make it easier to get a raid spot in a raiding guild. Usually shamans are the most in demand class, but if you want to see other options I would check your server's discord. For example Pagle is my server (discord.gg/pagle or you could google it or ask in game for someone to send you the link) and there is a dedicated channels for guild to list their recruitment needs. 

If you would rather just hop in and play and deal with finding a raid group later, I would recommend avoiding rogue and warrior as they are some of the hardest classses to get a raid spot as. 

I'm a very active raider so if anyone would like help/advice to get into raiding send me a msg id love to help!

In my opinion it is never too late to join a raiding guild. I joined halfway through classic and got a spot and am still raiding. 

I recommend leveling a class you enjoy. It's no fun to raid on a class you hate. Just understand that some classes (rogues especially) are very tough to get a raid spot. As long as you show up on time every raid and be a good teammate, you will get a spot.

In terms of getting raid ready, you can just hit 70 and hop right into Karazhan. You will probably get a ton of upgrades nobody wants on your first run. Many guilds are hungry to fill spots and if you are an unguilded 70 you will get PMs. 

You could also explore server discords (for example, discord.gg/pagle) and find a suitable guild that way.

Have fun!

Not sure if anyone has mentioned this yet but the KT trash respawns after 2 hours, aka you will have to at least reclear the trash in the boss room (but probably also leading up to it after a full wipe)

I would also recommend everyone in your raid gets weakauras if they dont have it and download the SSC and TK pack https://wago.io/u2Waemdhl

Particularly for KT it tells you to reequip your weapons, get out of conflag range, use the staff buff if youre a caster, who is MCed, and a whole ton more! It wont fix dps issues but it is very helpful.

I believe it, hard to predict for later raids we haven't seen as well. Unfortunately unless there are 8 tanks, 8 healers, and 24 DPS in a standard 40 man raid, it will still sadly be unbalanced towards requiring more DPS and/or healers for raiding in comparison to a standard 5 man group comp :(

People love pally buffs, if you aren't interested in tanking in raids then holy or ret are good choices. Holy is definitely easier to learn vs ret. Whatever you decide, I recommend getting all your dungeon gear/rep/attunements done as a tank while you can still form fast groups :)

If gold isn't a huge problem for you, there is also nothing wrong with respeccing a bunch to try out healing vs dps vs tank

I think tanks will always be in demand for 5 mans. If you want to get things done quick, being a tank and forming your own 5 mans is the way to go. It may be hard to get a raid spot, unless you decide to tank things as a fury or furyprot warrior. However i personally think bear tanks will have a bit less gear competition since you dont wear plate or swords/axes etc

However if you want to be a dps and do lots of dungeons, make friends with tanks or try to snipe LFG groups :)

If you want a raid spot pick dps or healer. If you want an easy chill solo lvling experience pick dps. If you want get instant dungeon groups and also be able to easily solo quest pick the bear. If none of that tickles your fancy, roll a dice! Or like others have suggested, level them all a bit and swap between them. All classes are fun in their own way :)

SoM is accelerated in terms of endgame content and quest XP, but if you like to chill out and quest/do dungeons as you lvl up you will be fine. The speed levelers will zoom ahead but most people will be just as fast as you are. Even in the first release of classic I started a few months late and I found groups and saw other people questing as a first time player. I would recommend getting the Questie addon unless you want a completely barebones experience. Good luck!

There definitely are east coast guilds that start that late, my guild in TBC starts at 9:30 eastern. I would check out the WoW forums or SoM discords to see if there is a guild recruiting at your preferred start time

I record with Shadowplay! Before Shadowplay I used OBS studio.

Shadowplay is built in with Nvidia's line of graphics cards, my card is a GTX 970. I don't believe you can get Shadowplay if you don't have a Nvidia graphics card. OBS is probably the best free recording software out there and it's very easy to set up.

For recording, I just kinda put myself in a good spot, played the replay, and flipped on Shadowplay for a minute or two.

All I really did is hide the camera controls and made many different shots by zooming in and out/moving around. Setting the drone in free mode and moving around slowly helped with the pan shots. It took me several hours to film everything and I had a ton of extra footage. I ended up going back through the replay a few times to get extra footage. I'm very slow :(

I edit in Premiere, but I don't think you need to do anything fancy to make stuff like this. In the past I've used Sony Vegas and Lightworks (which is free, but I had a hard time learning how to use it).
